The first half of this book is a complete waste of time. Genuinely, I don’t understand why there is so much singing and so many years before the actual adventure begins. It just drags on and on. I was so happy when strider showed up and the real story began. I honestly would tell people to read the first couple of chapters and then skip to like chapter 10, there’s nothing to miss.

I really like the movies of The Lord of the Rings, but the books didn't to it for me. They were too slow and too much description of everything (as other commenter have described). I love the story, but I prefer it in the movie format. I might have read the second one, but when I went to see how many pages it was, the last page jumped out at me and gave away the ending of book two. At that point, I gave up.

Basicallym some Hobbits go on a great big walk across a forest.
I think they meet some elves on the way.
God, it was boring.

I can imagine that if you read this as a small child, you might enjoy all the huge amount of surplus detail that exists in it (cos we obviously need to know the history of what Hobbits smoke instead of tobacco, JRR!) but on the various attempts as a teenager / adult to get through it, what I would have appreciated was a plot!

This will count as my reveiw for the series. Yawn... Granted I didn't read these books until after I had watched the movies but this is one case where the books were not nearly as good as the movies. I thought the plot moved too slow and had to really concentrate to keep myself from falling asleep. All in all I can say that I am glad the movies came out because otherwise I would have thought any who liked the books might need medication.

I respect this book for what it is: the first of its kind, totally innovative, an entire world created, these type of things. And I'm glad that I read it.

However, it was not really enjoyable to me. Honestly, I was just bored. I felt like for 450 pages, nothing really happened. I will continue reading the series, because I know that a lot of this was set up, but wow. I just felt like it was a chore or an assignment to get through this.

Eh.

This book is not as enjoyable, in my opinion, as The Hobbitt. Many sections of this book seemed to have a different purpose than telling a good story...the information conveyed was not done in a way that was entertaining. The communication seemed plodding in parts and more akin to a textbook or school history book rather than a book of fiction. Overall it was fine, and I am open to the possibility that after reading the other two books in this trilogy my opinion may change.

I'm definitely going to have to give this book another chance some time when I can be undisturbed. I had enjoyed Tolkien's "The Hobbit" so much that I was surprised to find it so difficult to get caught up in this story. For my part, there was entirely too much description of setting when I wanted to get on with the story. But, given the fact that his whole trilogy is so very well respected and popular, I am assuming I just wasn't in the right frame of mind at the time to enjoy it.

This is one of very few books that were not as good as the movie. This and the two sequels have weird asides with characters that only appear once and are never mentioned again. Legolas sings to a tree and a river and it's really random and kinda odd... I read this to prepare for the movie and was certain that they would match up. They don't match up... The first movie ends sometime in the beginning of the second book!

While considered a fantasy classic (and the "Harry Potter" of its time), Tolkien was more an academic than a fantasy writer, and it shows. Fascinated by languages (Tolkien and his brother made up several as children, these fantasy languages shaped the stories rather than the other way around. If you can handle pages of "Elvish" ballads, then go for it. Honestly, while you could be shunned by "true fantasy readers" for not tackling this series, I wouldn't hold it against you.

After reading The Hobbit and seeing the LOTR. Films I was looking forward to this book. It's taken me nearly 3 years to complete it. I started it when I was having a 1.5hours each way commute to work and found myself falling asleep every day with it in my hand. I must admit it was easier to follow while listening as well so I had the audio book downloaded. I didn't find it easy reading but listening was much better, I think I absorbed more.

Really, I don't see the big deal about it. This book took forever to get through, I just couldn't take it at large dosages. I was determined to read it because once I start, I don't want to leave it undone. I was glad I had a rough movie basis to take this on, I can't even remember the movie, just parts, so that helped me along with the book, but I am certainly glad I can now say I read the book, regardless of what i thought about it, I still read every word of it. Now, on to book 2.

I have attempted to read this novel at least half a dozen times, to no avail. I get to the Tom Bombadil portion of the novel, and stop reading. Every. Single. Time. It drags with unnecessary detail, and I cannot find enough redeeming qualities in the pages I do read to convince myself to push through until the end. It's really too bad. This series is right down my alley, and I feel like a fantasy series deserter for not being able to get through it.

Not a great book for an impatient man

I know Lord of the Rings is one of the best fantasy series, but perhaps I'm too unfamiliar with this genre, I was never able to really get into it.
I read the Hobbit and the Fellowship of the Rings, and I only seem to remember that the hobbits are always walking in the woods somewhere. They walk for days, and there is some action. Rinse, repeat. I do not have patience for a saga like this, and I gave up on the series after the first book.

I wish I had listened to the abridged version instead. The guy who read the book was very good, but there was just so much about the scenery. Just went on and on. It'd be like 45 minutes before some substantial dialogue would come up. Also Gandolph may be the most worthless wizard ever. Can't melt snow? Seriously? You can build fires but can't melt snow......

Anyway, the movie or maybe abridged version would be better. Not going to listen to the rest on tape. Just gonna watch the movies.

This is an excellent story and I want so much to love it because of that. Unfortunately, the story is buried under so much unnecessary detail that it sort of just gets lost. It's sort of like if someone tried to tell you how their day went and then spent six hours describing every detail of their alarm clock, including where and how it was made. After all that, you're really just tired and not interested in the rest of the story.

It was okay. Sorry to say this about a classic, but I didn't particularly enjoy this book. Maybe it's because I've seen the movies and already knew much of the plot line. Even listened to it twice, thinking maybe I missed something. I planned to read the whole Lord of the Rings trilogy this summer, but I think I'll wait until next summer to listen to the second part. My son insists that the second and third books are better.

Not by type of book. I listened to it only because I noted that it was the most popular fiction book ever. Boy, I would put it up there with another world famous book, Moby Dick. Count me out. I have learned to not go with the most popular titles. They have been losers, in my humble opinion, too often. Not saying the majority of the readers out there are losers just sayin' I don't like what most people like. I guess that's what I mean.

Lesson Today: Quintessential works of high fantasy/classics aren't my thing.

But overall, the first book of The Lord of the Rings was an interesting book. Yes, some people would find it boring, but I can see why others don't. Tolkien created not only a brilliant piece of literary but a new, fantastical world that captured millions of reader's hearts.

So yes, I'd still definitely read the next book.

Tolkien's writing can be summed up as "what not to do when writing engaging fiction". Studying his books really does teach you alot - as a negative example akin to Stephenie Meyer.
The world Tolkien creates is absolutely gorgeous and it is true that he was one of the forefathers of fantasy(he did NOT invent the genre, as fans like to claim), but we need to start facing one important fact: he wasn't a good writer in any way, shape or form.

Five weeks it took me to complete this. The amount of pages would normally take me a few days. Tolkien's writing style is so boring I completely lost the lust for reading. I get it, it's fantasy. You got to build a world. However, incorporate it into the story instead of just droning on about names, families and places that has no bearing on the story. And, again I know it's fantasy, but everything seems so artificial, especially some of the actions and interactions of the characters.

I thought it was OK. It wasn't outstanding or anything, but it was good. It took me a while to finish it, and it was kind of boring at times, mostly at the beginning of the book. There wasn't as much action as I had hoped. I saw the movies first, and those were a bit better, because they were a little bit more engaging then the book. I was hoping it would get better the farther I went, but it didn't. I was a little disappointed.

I loved reading the Hobbit and really looked forward to reading this book that so many people love. It just wasn't my kind of book. I wanted to like it and kept reading it hoping I would be drawn into like I as in the Hobbit. Oh well. I continued into the next book and just haven't been able to finish it. Maybe one of these days I am thinking it was because I listened to it as an audio book and it is one of those books that doesn't work to listen to.

Well, that was a bit painful. I listened to the audio and it took ENTIRELY too many weeks of my precious life. While I like fantasy, it just wasn't as fantastical enough! Nothing really happened: take the ring, hide the ring, SING, run away from black-clothed men on horses, SING, recruit others, stop getting tempted by the ring, SING, keep running away! I just couldn't really get into it ever. I think the movie is better, and more enjoyable.

There are several things I like about the book and other things I would change. I do like the idea, the fantasy and the interesting story line, but it was kind of slow. The chapters are very long and I am the type of person who likes shorter chapters. I also didn't like the fact that it took so long to get up to the climax of the book. Although it was kind of slow, I did enjoy imagining the book as a movie inside my head.

This is part 1 of 3 of the Lord of The rings. it is filled with monsters,elves and creepy people hiding in caves. It has several saddening events and betrayals. It is very descriptive of the setting. This book is a very tedious thing to read. It takes up a whole page just describing one little thing. This book really broke my patience. I was just trying to burn through the pages because it was so boring. I didn't have any intention on reading the second one.

Su lentitud, desde mi punto de vista lo hace muy difícil de leer. Lo leí hace muchos años junto con el segundo de la saga pero fué imposible terminar el tercero. Su fantasía no me impresiona y me resulta un poco agobiante.
Ni siquiera sé qué pasó con el dichoso anillo y no es algo que me haya quitado el sueño nunca. Me gusta la fantasía, la ciencia ficción, pero de este libro no tengo un buen recuerdo...

I thought the first 300 pages were boring, almost insufferable. I could stand the unnecessary and excessive details, but the story was lacking so much. It felt like all Frodo and his companions did was to eat dinner with friends. Boring!!
But then, after Rivendell, yes!
I liked the last 100 pages and I really hope that’s how the later books are... not sure when I’ll read them though. Hopefully soon. :-)

I started reading this book in September 2019 and I finally managed to finish it in the end of March of 2020. It was so hard for me to get through it and I even skimmed through most parts. But I am one of those who only reads one book at a time and I was too stubborn to quit, so I missed out of a lot of reading for this half a year because this book took me too long.
I can deal with the movies but this was terribly boring.

Updated review as i realized the previous version I’d listened to was drastically edited. Still One of a few books where I actually enjoyed the movie more than the book because this book is dreadfully boring. There are only a couple fantasy authors I’ve read and enjoyed, namely Michael J Sullivan. I’m about 75% of the way through and have officially given up... I’ll stick with the movies, thanks.

Nunca, pero nunca, me había demorado tanto en leer un libro.

Debo decir que entiendo porque es una historia tan amada y famosa, y admito que me encantó la historia.

Pero he de decir que pensé que nunca iba a terminar el libro.

Es una historia muy interesante con diferentes personajes.

Pero me parece que hay muuuuchas cosas que se habrían podido omitir o hacer una mención más corta (como lo de Tom bombaldi).

En fin, me gustó pero fue demasiado para mí.

2025 re-read: *2.5 stars rounded down*
Standing by my previous review from 6 years ago. Unpopular opinion, but I don’t really like LOTR.


2019 review: *3 stars*
Okay, unpopular opinion, but this was hard for me to get into! It had such a slow pace that it doesn't really count as a page-turner. Frodo was just walking through the woods for sooooooo many pages. Maybe I'll read it again in the future.

I’m so upset I disliked this book as much as I did.
One one hand Tolkien’s world-building is INSANE and the book is a testament to his intelligence and creativity but on the other hand his way of describing this amazing world, history and adventure that he has thought up is extremely extremely dull.
Everything about the world, the narrative, the tropes and the individual characters is so strong that that it makes the articulation of these things even more disappointing

This book has so many ups and down. No really. It's mostly about hobbits going up hills and down hills. And eating. And then they stop somewhere for a short time and do it all over again. If you like scenery described in excruciatingly vivid detail, this is the book for you.

I'm halfway through it, and I don't know how I'm going to finish it. I'll be back to finish the review.

I'm giving up at The Ring Goes South. I am not interested enough to continue.

While it’s easy to recognize the brilliance and influence Tolkien has had on the fantasy genre, I found this first installment to the LOTR to be somewhat slow at times, when it didn’t need to be. I also wished there had been some more growth from the characters throughout their journey. With that being said, I am happy to have read this book because it’s an important work of literature, I just think maybe it wasn’t really for me.

I have nothing against this book. I know it is a classic along with a lot of Tolkien's other works. I just had a hard time getting into this book and staying interested. I think the problem was I tried to read this after having watched the movie and could not get the comparisonout of my head. Great book but just wasn't for me.

Compared to The Hobbit, I found Fellowship of the Ring to go so slow. It's a wonderfully rich world, but there was way too much detail clogging up the pace of the story. I realize many people love the book because it contains so much detail, but for me it got in the way of the story rather than enhancing it.

I love the idea of Tolkien's stories. The actual text of the book -- the way that Tolkien goes on about descriptions ... well. I could blame my ADD, but I just can't get through reading them. I fall asleep when he goes off about the trees, or the history of the history of the cousin of the eldest dwarf.

I RESPECT his work. But I just cannot read it.

I realize it's faintly sacrilegious to give this book only two stars, but I was bored to tears by it, to the point that I'm not entirely sure I got all the way through it. I appreciate the genius and complexity of the world and all that, but oh my goodness, Frodo spends so much time walking. I really, truly, honestly thought it made a better movie. So shoot me.

I read this for a speed-reading course over the summer, which means homework over the summer. More homework and work than I had because of work and the bridging program. This made my reading experience pretty bad. It is a very boring book with lots of description. I almost died of boredom. Ahh, there is like two action scenes.

Honestly, I think these books are amazing but I couldn't get past this one. Tolkien had such a great imagination but his descriptions took so long sometimes that I got lost. I think people should at least conquer the first one. It is worth it in the end to just get inside this tale through your own imagination.

I have nothing against the story here: It's undoubtedly skillfully put together. However, I took a unusually long time to read it, and that is because everything is described in great detail, so more than action, you often get a (unnecesary and/or long) description of the places, the people, and the ancestors they have - and I had problems remembering all of those.

This started out okay but it is just not keeping my attention. I want to like it and it is well-written, but I just can't get into it. All of his weird spellings and songs just irritate me and it moves really slowly. I also don't like any of the hobbit characters, which seems like just about all of the book.

LoTR is my favorite movie of all time so I thought I had to read the books. But I was disappointed and I don't see the fuss about it at all. It was boring from the beginning to the end and I had to fight against my will to stop reading. I read it once,just for the sake of it,but I will never read it again and stick with the movie(s)...

Hobbits in search of a plot–that ought to be the title of this aimless story. I think Tolkien started out with no plan in mind, sort of like Frodo and his fellow hobbits, following the road, wondering where it would take him. I know the action heats up later on, but I don’t have the patience to stick with it. Nobody’s making me read it this time. There’s so much good literature out there!

Honestly, I could not finish the book. It was an Odyssey-journey-novel, and I did not find the journey, the challenge, or the characters compelling enough to keep reading. I have not yet watched the movies, as I wanted to read the books, first. Now I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place. My apologies to Dave. I'll try again, someday.

I felt like they were pioneer children- all they do is walk and walk and walk and sing and walk and walk and then something happens and then they walk and walk.... you get the idea. I have been told that these books get better as they go, but I just could not get into the story... maybe I should try again.

o.k., now let me explain why I gave the rest of these Lord of the Rings books a bad rating. I really liked the story line, but there was just to much blah blah blah in between. I found it tedious to read. The Hobbit was excellent. I don't believe I ever finished the last of the books because I just couldn't take anymore. Too slow moving. Honestly, I thought the movies were better.

This book is really for someone who likes to read for the adventure of it. It goes on and on and there is so much singing i thought it should have been a musical. The story line is very good and if you cut out about 200 pages of the book... it makes for a really good read.

all n all this is just not the kind of book for me. Its going to be a VERY long time before i read the next two...

This book is important, but it isn't good. Tolkien introduced many ideas and tropes to the general public, but others have built on his work.

Every idea and Trope explored in Tolkien has been done better many, many times by many, many authors. If you want to understand fantasy roots, then you can read Tolkien otherwise, read something more interesting.

This book has over half a million ratings on Goodreads, with an average of 4.22 stars, so I had to see what was so great about it. I can now say that I read it, but I honestly did not enjoy it. I found it very boring and had to force myself to finish it. I was constantly flipping ahead to see how many pages I had left.

Hmm...the major thing that stuck out to me when reading the book was the really exciting action taking place in the book juxtaposed with Tolkien's incrediby dull description of it. I really liked the story itself, but I just did not like how he wrote it all. Unfortunately, I thought the movies were way way way better.

A classic certainly (and for good reason) but not my cup of tea. The first part is far too long and as Tolkien chooses archetypes rather than characters for the most part, in order to align more closely with the Medieval romance tradition, I found it difficult to engage with as a modern reader. (The exception is of course the Hobbits, Tolkien's concession to modernism.)

Too many songs and silly things going on in here for it to keep my attention. Loved The Hobbit in high school, but this book was a bit too much of the fantasy world for my tastes at the time I read it almost four years ago. Perhaps it's to be revisited later on down the road. I'll keep my copy for now.

I get it. He inspired a genre. But, it just wasn't my style. When the plot actually moved, the book read fast. Most of the time, however, the plot didn't move. Not a lot of character development outside of Frodo and Sam, and minimal there. Far too much time on pastoral descriptions of the landscape. If you're into that, this was fantastic. If you're not, then bummer.

I love "The Hobbit" and I loved all the LotR movies, so I thought that the books would be a no-brainer. I was actually excited to start on these books, but I just couldn't get into Fellowship. I guess these are another one of those things where you either get it you don't and I just don't. I tried, I really did. I don't hate the books; I just couldn't break into them.

I love the movie!But the book just wasn't for me. It was still a great story and it was well written, but it's not my normal style of book and I believe that is why I didn't like it as much. To me it was kind of boring, but even the more interesting parts couldn't keep my interest. I'm still going to try to read the second book though.

I know Tolkien is supposed to be classic and everything and I'm sure he is but I just couldn't get Into the book like I did the movies. As a true lover of the fantasy genre I did push myself through all 3 books in this trilogy but it was really hard to. I don't know why I didn't enjoy it much I just didn't.

Loomulikult super lugu, aga lugeda ma seda l6puni ei suutnud. Ma jätsin ta pooleli, kuna k6ik oli kudiagi väga korduv ja igav. Possibly one of the first times I've liked a movie more than its corresponding book. I know that it is unfair to measure a book to its movie all the time but usually it is the exact opposite and that is notable. It was ok - there were some interesting tidbits that were left out but ultimately the story didn't move very quickly and was a fairly repetitive.

I have such a hard time reading these books that it's just hard for me to enjoy them. There were good parts where it picked up, but definitely a lot of walking....still walking....let's hear more about walking... Not altogether too bad; there were parts that made me laugh, but if I wasn't in a reading class I probably wouldn't have finished it for another month.

I love the storyline and the movie version of this, particularly the full-length director's cut, kicked ass. In print however, Tolkien just cannot seem to stop describing things. There's a fine line between necessary descriptions and forcing the reader's imagination to see what you see. Tolkien not only crosses that line, he crosses it with an army of Uruk-hai to try and obliterate it.

A great book for the summer days, well, evenings and nights too. But I have to say, if you have watched the movie then there is no need to read the book. It's one of the rare times that the movie is superior to the book. peter Jackson took the greatness of "LORD: The Fellowship of the Ring" and turned it to perfection!

I really wanted to like this, I really did. I just could not get into it. The book just seemed so two-dimensional, with the characters all following tropes and following the classic good vs evil story. While I understand why people like it (the rich world building, adventure etc.), I just didn't seem to enjoy it.

As much as I try to get into the LOTR series or The Hobbit, I just can't. I will always he a Harry Potter fan and the writing and plots of these series just do not interest me as much. I just find it boring and slow which causes me to quickly lose interest. I have tried to read this series multiple times and quit every time.

The story is good he created a wonderful world with several century's worth of backstory. But it kept interrupting what was happening in the present it was really hard to get through the book. Its good that he had backstory but you didn't need to be bashed over the head with it. it was like taking a history class, and I read to enjoy the book NOT take a history class.

Monta kertaa on tämä teos tullut aloitettua ja nyt sain sen loppuun äänikirjana. Ei se huono ollut, mutta en vain löytänyt sitä syvintä olemusta tästä teoksesta. Elokuvakin on tullut katsottua, eikä sekään ole kiinnostanut ensimmäistä katselukertaa enempää, joten tuskin tulee tartuttua kirjalliseen versioon.

Pitänee kuunnella myös seuraavat osat, jos ne olisivat viihdyttävämpiä.

Pros:

Somewhat engaging.
Coherent storyline.
Nice character and world development.

Cons:

World-view is false: Evil is shown as central, organized, and un-dying. Good is shown as blind luck happening here and there. That is completely false. In reality, good is central, organized and almighty, and eternal while evil is deceived and temporary.

It just dragged on and on and on and on.... So many weird and unique names, its easy to get confused and lost and therefor easy to stop caring. And when one stops caring the book gets boring... and the small amount of curiosity in the plot is not enough to read the next, but to skip straight to the movies or wikipedia.

Oh the walking. I thought the movie was long, but they really cut back. Also, sooo many characters I'd never heard of. And the poems. So long some times. I skipped a couple. It was alright. It did not affect my heart. Well written sue but not something I emotionally cling to. I know what happens, I was not moved. But one down two to go.

not my style of writing at all. the whole book was about a leg of a long journey. i finished it and the 2nd was the same journey! too slow for me and i didnt care for the writing. which stinks becasue everyone else loves this series! lol. maybe i will try again some day. btw - hated the hobbit too.

I enjoyed the overall story, but I couldn't keep the characters straight and WAY TOO MUCH battling and the scenes lasted WAY TOO LONG. After reading about Mr. Tolkien I know this may have been cathartic for him after World War I, but I had to watch the movie to figure everything out in the end. Also I'm not a male. ^_^

De verdad que lo intenté, pero fui incapaz de acabar este libro. A pesar de que me encantan las películas y la historia en general, el libro se me ha hecho pesadísimo. Llegué a la página 300 y aún no pasaba nada, ni me había acercado a los personajes, ni nada de nada. Será un libro bueno, pero yo no pude con él

Wasn't a fan of the poems/songs and lengthy descriptions of old lands and histories not really related to the direct storyline. I understand the author created a whole other world in these books, but it is just too fantastical and irrelevant to keep my interest. I'm hoping the series picks up the pace a bit in the next book...

I wanted to love it, but it was not happening. At any point. I tried to slowly enjoy the journey. I liked the films and I like high fantasy. I got through the toughest parts of ASOIAF to enjoy the whole ride for what it is. But for whatever reason, this giant book did not do anything for me. I might have been more interested if everyone except our elven royalty were ladies, but I doubt it.

I did it. I finished. The last 100 pages I just kinda skimmed through but shhhh. I really didn't love this book. I know, I'm sorry! I understand its importance to modern literature I just didn't really connect with any of the characters and Tolkien likes describing every piece of moss on every single rock and it annoys me. Sorry not sorry. Surprised I'm not giving it 1 star but hey.

I wanted to like this book and I forced myself to read on thinking that eventually I would get into it, but I frequently felt bored and disinterested. Every chapter felt like a lengthy description of the landscape, a sprinkling of songs, and maybe one page of eventful action. I kept waiting for something to happen. I can see why some enjoy the book, but this one just isn't my cup of tea.

I struggled with this book! I really wanted to like it but found Tolkiens writing very hard to get into! I eventualy stopped reading shortly after starting the chapter 'A journey in the dark' & it has sat on my bookshelf ever since. I hate to have not finished it but I read for the enjoyment of getting lost in a book and I just didnt find that joy with this book!

Lord of the Rings...where the films are better than the books.

I've read this once in German 15 years ago and 'just now' in English to my daughter at bedtime. It is, I hate to say it, dull. Especially the first 200 or so pages. I remember it getting better, but god, one has to have stamina and willpower.

Alltså det är en extremt bra historia och värld. Det helt otroligt hur Tolkien kom på allting. Difficult to distinguish one voice from another at times. Made it hard to follow dialogs. I know the Lord of the Rings is one of those books that’s just a classic and it’s so good, but honestly it’s quite bad. I think if I read it when I’m older I will enjoy it more. Lots of the language is quite confusing. But the worst thing was that Tolkien drawls on about something when there is no need to. It took me so long to actually finish because I was getting so bored.

I know I am probably going to get my homeschool card revoked, but this one falls under the category of “I’m glad I read it, but I have never been so glad to be done with a book in my life.” Long, boring. I just couldn’t get into it. It was just one of those books that you’re “supposed”to read, so I did, but I will not be reading the rest. I just don’t get all the hype.

I feel so bad giving this book a low rating, but it literally took 4 months for me to get through. I found myself re-reading parts without even noticing. However, I did enjoy it. It has a nice vibe and I love the coziness of it all - Sam has to be my favourite character in the series aside from Legolas, he's just so lovable!

No fue para mi🙃. Admiro mucho la forma de escribir del autor, pero sinceramente no es que es tediosa, sino que se me hacía muy lenta y sentí que no pasó nada. Se nota que Tolkien lo escribió sobre la marcha.

Rescato mucho las descripciones y el mundo que creo pero la verdad me falto la acción.

I listened to this as an audio book and became enormously frustrated at all the songs. It became stressful waiting for the next one to arrive. I eventually started skipping them and it was like a weight of my shoulders and I could begin to enjoy the story.

1.75⭐️ I love the movies and the creativity is great but it’s very slow going most of the time and and the version I have the font is tiny so it takes ages to read a page. i wanted to like this book so badly but i couldn’t help feeling bored and sleepy reading it. it was very slow for my liking. the characters are alright. overall, it’s a big meh. i’m not sure if i’m disappointed in myself for not liking it or in the book itself. hoping book 2 is better. yes i’m still gonna read book 2. wish me luck.

DNF

Soooooo boring. I made it to the end of book 1 (Rivendell).

I feel a little bit terrible for NOT liking this book as much as everyone else seems too. Infact, I don't think I even finished it. The language is very beautiful, but for me it was just such a slow read with pages and pages of description.
I'm trying to decide if I should try to read it again...

This first book in the trilogy moves very slowly. I thought I was never going to get past Tom Bombadil (I probably misspelled that). Anyway, skim the boring parts and keep going because The Two Towers and Return of the King are much, much better.

Ari and I were reading this together and we just don't get it. Their 300-plus page journey could have taken one chapter to complete. We bought all the books in the series; however, it doesn't look like we will be reading beyond this one.

It's hard for me to stimulate my imagination through reading this book. Perhaps it is a lot easier just watching the movies. Anyway, it is one of my favorite. I think Tolkien was succeed to build a 'new world'.

As much as I LOVE the story and appreciate Tolkien's creativity and eloquence, the whole Lord of the Rings series needs to be seriously abridged for it to be completely enjoyable. Talk about long-winded. I would vote for the movies any day over reading those books again.

I should love these books. I know I should. I tried really hard. I can't do it. I feel like a failure. I think it is the writing style. It just doesn't do it for me. This may be the only time that I ever liked a movie more than I liked a book (yikes).

UGH! I only read it because I challenged myself to finish it before watching the movie. I couldn't STAND the language! Trying to follow all the lineage was torture! I literally fell asleep every 10 pages!

I love LOTR, but let's be serious - Tolkien doesn't figure out what he's doing till the last third of this book. Until then, it wanders, it has annoying interludes, and the characters are complete idiots.

This is ok maybe it is the language but I would get lost all the time and not understand what I he was talking about so this was ok for me but there are some really fun parts that were left out of the movie which is unfortunate but it was tough to get through all of the books.

I love the story of LOTR; I just think that Tolkien's writing style leaves a lot to be desired. There's no questioning the impact of this tale on the literary world; however, this is one of the few times where I think the movies were vastly superior to the books.

As a person who likes fantasy that takes us into a whole different world, I must say, I like the writing, and I like the world JRR Tolkien created, but the story is sort of dull. There are instances where the characters get into serious trouble, but that doesn't come until much later in the book. Until then, we only hear of trouble and it's a lot of preparation and a lot of sightseeing. That's another thing about this first book in the series, it is about a bunch of friends who liv ea quaint life that go out into the uncomfortable woods, but meet a lot of eccentric people as well. Sometimes they're larger than life, sometimes they can save you from horrible forest creatures. I think their journey could have been much more suspenseful, though, and the characters they meet much more affected by the ring and therefore cause them trouble. I liked the later part of the book, where we get to see Gandalf use his powers, and the cave scenes are just as frightening here as they were in the film.

If you like a lot of sightseeing in a fantastical realm, this book will be enjoyable! If you like action and lots of drama amongst characters, then you will have a tough time getting through this.

This book(since like any other classic, many who it inspired no doubt did *not* read the whole trilogy, but just the part of the first book) inspired much of the 20st century greats, from Star Trek to Final Fantasy to Sean Kennedy. But it just didn't speak to me. It's written by a man, not a god, for sure. Tolkien set the bar - the 21st century must get over this work in particular if we are to be worthy of being his intellectual progeny.

Perhaps part of it is that I saw the movie before reading the book. I do wonder how it would have been if it were the other way around. It was a long time ago that I did so and I didn't remember much of the detail/plot. I *do not* recall naked hobbits prancing around in Tom Bombadil's place, or nearly as much singing though and I wonder if that's something that new zealand/american/MPAA/late 20th/early 21st century culture is blinded to in retrospect because of it.
